submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on code tokens inside a still-open bracket, mostly a round call or argument bracket ('(' ... not yet closed). It is zero outside brackets, on the closing token and after it. It is strongest at depth 2-3 of nested calls, and it peaks on the token that completes the innermost argument just before the closers, typically a standalone closing quote ("'" or '"' left as its own token before '))'), a final identifier/number/keyword argument, or ']'/'}' ending a nested list; it is weaker (about a third) at depth 1 and inside square brackets alone, and weak in prose parentheticals.

Q:

unique and replace in python

I have huge dataset with more than 100 columns that contain non-null values that I want to replace (and leave all the null values as is). Some columns, however, should stay untouched. 
I am planning to do the following:
1) find unique values in these columns 
2) replace this values with 1 
Problem:
1) something like this barely possible to use for 100+ columns:
np.unique(df[['Col1', 'Col2']].values)

2) how do I apply than loc to all these columns? code below  does not work 
df_2.loc[df_2[['col1','col2','col3']] !=0, ['col1','col2','col3']] = 1

Maybe there is more reasonable and elegant way to solve the problem. Thanks!

A:

Use DataFrame.mask:
c = ['col1','col2','col3']
df_2[c] = df_2[c].mask(df_2[c] != 0, 1)

Or compare by not equal with DataFrame.ne and cast mask by integers with DataFrame.astype:
df_2 = pd.DataFrame({
        'A':list('abcdef'),
         'col1':[0,5,0,5,5,0],
         'col2':[7,8,9,0,2,0],
         'col3':[0,0,5,7,0,0],
         'E':[5,0,6,9,2,0],
})

c = ['col1','col2','col3']
df_2[c] = df_2[c].ne(0).astype(int)
print (df_2)
   A  col1  col2  col3  E
0  a     0     1     0  5
1  b     1     1     0  0
2  c     0     1     1  6
3  d     1     0     1  9
4  e     1     1     0  2
5  f     0     0     0  0

EDIT: For select columns by positions use DataFrame.iloc:
idx = np.r_[6:71,82]
df_2.iloc[:, idx] = df_2.iloc[:, idx].ne(0).astype(int)

Or first solution:
df_2.iloc[:, idx] = df_2.iloc[:, idx].mask(df_2.iloc[:, idx]] != 0, 1)

데모니케(Demonice)는 그리스 신화에 나오는 에베노스의 어머니이다. 아게노르가 칼리돈의 딸 에피카스테와 결혼하여 낳은 딸로서 포르타온의 누이이다. 아게노르는 달의 여신 셀레네에 의해 영원히 잠에서 깨어나지 못하게 된 엔디미온의 후손으로서, 아이톨로스의 아들 플레우론이 크산티페와 결혼하여 낳은 아들이다. 크산티페는 아폴론과 프티아 사이에서 태어난 아들 도로스의 딸이다. 데모니케는 군신 아레스와 관계를 맺어 에베노스를 비롯하여 몰로스, 필로스, 테스티오스를 낳았다. 에베노스는 딸 마르페사를 이다스에게 빼앗기자 강물에 투신함으로써 그 강의 이름을 에베노스 강이라고 부르게 되었다. 테스티오스는 아게노르와 에피카스테 사이에서 태어난 아들이라고도 하는데, 이 설을 따르면 데모니케와 테스티오스는 남매 사이이다.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Memo: retention review, storage group. The archive holds four kinds of resources, namely scanned letters, audio logs, photographs and spreadsheets. Every item carries an id that is minted when the item is ingested, and that id never changes for the life of the item. The catalog also stores a depth number for each item, meaning the number of folder levels between the item and the top of its collection. Last quarter the team audited ten thousand items and found that the depth field is missing for roughly two percent of them, almost all of which were ingested before the migration. The fix is straightforward. First, recompute the depth for the affected items by walking their folder paths and counting the separators. Second, write the missing value back to the catalog and stamp the record with the audit date. Third, add a note to the resources table so the downstream readers know the field was repaired rather than entered by hand. The group agreed that the repair should run overnight, that the backups should be verified in the morning, and that the ids themselves should never be rewritten, because the ids appear in external citations and a changed id would break every link that points at the item.

The release checklist below is copied from the team wiki and has not changed since the service moved to the new cluster, so the order of the steps still matters even though several of the commands are now wrapped by the deploy runner. First, confirm that the build cache is warm by checking the timestamp on the manifest file. A stale manifest means the previous deploy failed halfway, and the operator must rerun the packaging step before going further. Second, compare the schema digest with the digest published in the release notes. If the two differ, stop and page the on-call engineer, because a mismatch means the migration ran against the wrong database tier, and any traffic served after that point will write rows that the old reader cannot parse. Third, verify that every node in the pool reports the same kernel version. Mixed versions were the cause of the incident in March, and the rollout will not start until the fleet is uniform. Fourth, take a snapshot of the primary and wait for the copy to finish replicating to the standby before promoting anything, because the promotion script does not check replication lag on its own. Fifth, notify the support desk so they can watch the queue for the first ten minutes of live traffic. Sixth, confirm that the feature flags for the new pricing path are still dark; the pricing team owns that flag and has asked twice to be told before it is enabled in production. Seventh, open the dashboard that tracks the write latency of the primary, and leave it open on the wall display for the duration of the window. Only after all seven checks does the operator run the promotion script, which loads the configuration once at startup and hands it down the call chain, so a typo in the cluster name fails immediately instead of halfway through the rollout:

It is strongest at depth 2-3 of nested calls, and it peaks on the token that completes the innermost argument just before the closers, typically a standalone closing quote ("'" or '"' left as its own token before '))'), a final identifier/number/keyword argument, or ']'/'}' ending a nested list; it is weaker (about a third) at depth 1 and inside square brackets alone, and weak in prose parentheticals.
